$comment: Which changes the auto-merge workflow may merge on its own, and which need the owner. Read by .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml (Gate 6) from the base branch, never from the PR, so a PR cannot loosen the policy it is judged by. A rule matches when any changed file (both names on a rename) matches one of its paths: a path ending in / matches everything under it, any other path matches that file only, and a leading **/ matches at any depth. decision 'owner' means the owner merges by hand. mode 'enforce' holds the merge; mode 'observe' only logs that it would have, for trying a rule before relying on it.

rules.description: Workflow files. GitHub refuses to let the workflow's own token merge a PR that changes them, so the merge would fail anyway; holding it says why. This also covers a PR that edits the gate itself, which a PR's own run would otherwise judge by its edited copy.
The review process itself: this policy, the reviewer registry, agents, skills, commands, scripts and settings. One final review should not be able to change how the next PR is reviewed or merged.
